classification.difficultyReason: Infer missing regions in a three-set Venn diagram from overlapping totals, then distinguish inclusive union from an exclusive pairwise intersection.

content.prompt:
Of 15 courier companies:

9 offer a local service ($L$), 7 offer an interstate service ($S$) and 6 offer an international service ($I$).

2 companies offer all three services, 3 offer both local and interstate services, 5 offer only local services and 1 offers only an international service.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Complete the Venn diagram to display the given information.

spec.description: Universal-set rectangle with three overlapping circles: L above, S below left and I below right. All eight regions have room for handwritten counts.
spec.mathematics: Three sets with all pairwise and triple intersections and an outside region.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the set labels are visible; all supplied solution counts are omitted.

answer.short: $L$ only: $5$; $S$ only: $2$; $I$ only: $1$; $L$ and $S$ only: $1$; $L$ and $I$ only: $1$; $S$ and $I$ only: $2$; all three: $2$; none: $1$.
answer.worked:
Place $2$ in the intersection of all three sets, $5$ in $L$ only and $1$ in $I$ only.

$L$ and $S$ only: $3-2=1$.

$L$ and $I$ only: $9-5-1-2=1$.

$S$ and $I$ only: $6-1-1-2=2$.

$S$ only: $7-1-2-2=2$.

None: $15-(5+2+1+1+1+2+2)=1$.

spec.description: Completed three-set Venn diagram with all eight region counts.
spec.mathematics: L only 5; S only 2; I only 1; LS only 1; LI only 1; SI only 2; triple intersection 2; outside 1.

children.label: b
children.prompt: If a courier is chosen at random from the 15, find these probabilities:

answer.worked:
Count every region in either $L$ or $S$, including their overlap.
$$\begin{align*}n(L\text{ or }S)&=5+1+1+2+2+2\\&=13\\P(L\text{ or }S)&=\frac{13}{15}\end{align*}$$

There is $1$ company in both $L$ and $S$ but outside $I$.
$$P(L\text{ and }S\text{ only})=\frac{1}{15}$$
